newsitem.title: USA: Tosco Q2 impacted by margins, acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Tosco Q2 impacted by margins, acquisitions.

text.p: Tosco Corp said on Thursday its net income for the second quarter of 1997 was $67.1 million on sales of $3.2 billion against $49.6 million on sales of $2.4 billion, reflecting its acquisition of new businesses from Unocal and Circle K as well as refinery margins.

"Tosco's second quarter results were impacted by the dramatic decline in West Coast refining margins during May and June. Margins on the East Coast, Tosco's other principal refining market, were good throughout most of the period. Retail margins were also good during the quarter on all of Tosco's marketing areas," Tosco chairman and chief executive Thomas O'Malley said in a statement.
Tosco reported second earnings per share of $0.43, compared with $0.41 in the year ago period.
Net income increased to $67.1 million from $49.6 million, reflecting the acquisition of 2,500 convenience stores from Circle K on May 30, 1996.

Tosco said it is integrating the operations of its recently acquired 76 Products assets with its existing system, which led to some "transition expenses" in the second quarter. The transition is on schedule and on budget, O'Malley said.

When Tosco acquired the 76 Products assets from Unocal on March 31, 1997, the company said it will sell non-core assets. So far, the company has sold $60 million of these assets, including oil tankers and a heating oil distributorship, it said.

Tosco said it is continuing to tie together its newly acquired Rodeo-Santa Maria Refining Complex with its existing Avon Refinery, renaming the facilities San Francisco Area Refinery and placing them under common operating management.
Earlier this month, Tosco announced that Rodeo's lubricants base stock manufacturing facilities will be shut down in the third quarter.
Tosco said it expects the San Francisco refining integration project will be completed by next spring.
